title: Chapter VII
focus: the Plaza and the death car

teacherSummary.text: On the hottest day of summer Gatsby and Nick lunch with the Buchanans; Tom realizes Daisy loves Gatsby. They drive to the city, Tom in Gatsby's yellow car. At the Plaza, Tom exposes Gatsby's bootlegging; Daisy says she loved both. Driving home in Gatsby's car, Daisy hits Myrtle, who runs into the road, killing her. Gatsby waits outside the Buchanans' house; Nick sees Tom and Daisy conspiring.

context.history: The Plaza Hotel on Fifth Avenue was a landmark of luxury. Tom's charge that Gatsby and Wolfshiem 'bought up a lot of side-street drug-stores' reflects a real Prohibition practice: pharmacies could sell alcohol on prescription and served as fronts for bootlegging. Cars were new and lightly regulated; traffic deaths rose sharply in the 1920s.

significance: The climax: in one afternoon Gatsby's dream is exposed as resting on crime and on a past he cannot erase, and the car, the novel's symbol of status and danger, becomes a weapon. Responsibility for Myrtle's death begins to be shifted from the careless to the dreamer.

segments.script: The Plaza Hotel on Fifth Avenue was a landmark of luxury. Tom's charge that Gatsby and Wolfshiem 'bought up a lot of side-street drug-stores' reflects a real Prohibition practice: pharmacies could sell alcohol on prescription and served as fronts for bootlegging. Cars were new and lightly regulated; traffic deaths rose sharply in the 1920s. The climax: in one afternoon Gatsby's dream is exposed as resting on crime and on a past he cannot erase, and the car, the novel's symbol of status and danger, becomes a weapon. Responsibility for Myrtle's death begins to be shifted from the careless to the dreamer. Setting: The hottest day of summer; the Plaza Hotel confrontation. Characterization: Tom exposes Gatsby; Daisy cannot deny she loved Tom. Symbolism: Daisy's voice "full of money." Watch for the green light: The light at the end of Daisy's dock: Gatsby's dream, distant and unreachable, and finally the "orgiastic future" that recedes before everyone. In this chapter: “I went with them out to the veranda. On the green Sound, stagnant in the heat, one small sail crawled slowly toward” (Chapter VII, paragraph 68).
